If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for downward bias.  
If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast peak to later horizon (days 15–25) and reduce slope steepness.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (days 20–30) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid-horizon to avoid false optimism.  
If sentiment is negative and price is rising, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon to offset sentiment-driven underestimation.
